svg.text: The music theory behind Dario's sequencer
How one firing step becomes a note — and why four independent lanes always agree.
Which steps fire, how dense they
are, and how long the lane's loop
Which note each firing step plays
— and how that pitch moves over
One note, or a chord built on it
Rhythm, melody and harmony are decided independently — the classic orthogonal split. Everything below resolves
one firing step of the pitch and voicing layers.
RUNNING PITCH (MIDI NOTE · NAME) — WORKED EXAMPLE IN KEY A, NATURAL MINOR
The lane's starting pitch — OCTAVE moves it in whole 12-semitone steps.
MANUAL, WALK, TURING, EUCLID or TECHNO sets a per-step offset in semitones.
This bar's chord degree in semitones, read off the scale's 7-note parent.
With ARP on, the step takes the next tone of that chord instead of the root.
SNAP TO THE GLOBAL SCALE + KEY
The nearest note of the one global scale wins, and a tie rounds down. Nothing can leave the key.
82 (A#) sits exactly between A and B, so it resolves down to 81 (A5). In-scale degrees are lit; the rest are never played.
The snapped note plays as it is. With a progression
running, the same melodic shape is re-rooted onto each
new chord — a bassline or lead that follows the
CHORD stacks the other tones on the root; INV then
lifts the lowest of them an octave for smoother
Diatonic shapes (DIA / DIA7 / DIA9) stack by scale degree, so each chord's quality — minor here — is taken from the key rather
than chosen by hand. The fixed shapes (MAJ, MIN, SUS4, 5TH…) plane one interval set onto every root, and are allowed to step
outside the key as a deliberate colour.
The pitch is settled. The STEPS page now shapes how long the note lasts, how hard it hits, how it sits against
the grid, and whether it ties into the step that follows.
Because every lane snaps into the same Scale + Key,
four independent rhythms can never clash. The interest
comes from rhythm, register and loop length, not from
PROG advances one chord per lane loop, so LENGTH and
DIV/MULT decide how fast the harmony moves. Same
progression with different STEPS gives related but
